summary: Palestine has no border control of its own — every route into the West Bank runs through Israeli-controlled crossings (Ben Gurion Airport or the Allenby Bridge from Jordan), so Israel's entry rules determine who gets in; the Palestinian Authority issues no visas, and Gaza is effectively closed to travelers.

fee.notes: Application fee, paid online; Israel's Population and Immigration Authority says it cannot be refunded after you apply.

source.name: Israel Population and Immigration Authority — About ETA-IL

applyWindow.text: The Population and Immigration Authority recommends submitting the application at least 72 hours before departure to Israel.

source.name: Population and Immigration Authority — Apply for an ETA-IL: start your application

fee.notes: The Foreign Ministry's 2026 consular tariff for a B/2 visitor visa at Israeli missions: USD 32 or €28, charged in local currency.

source.name: Israel Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Fees for consular services (B/2 Visitor Visa, 2026)

passportValidity.text: Israel controls all crossings into the West Bank. Its Population and Immigration Authority requires a passport valid for at least 3 months from the date of arrival.

source.name: Israel Population and Immigration Authority — About ETA-IL (eligibility conditions)

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states an insurance requirement for visa-exempt visitors entering through Israel on an ETA-IL. Applicants for Israel's eVisa-B2 tourist visa must show health insurance valid for the whole visit.

source.name: Israel Population and Immigration Authority — eVisa-B2 tourist visa: required documents

onwardTicket.text: Applicants for Israel's eVisa-B2 tourist visa must upload a round-trip ticket. No official source we could read states a return-ticket requirement for visa-exempt visitors on an ETA-IL; the UK says visitors may face lengthy questioning and baggage searches when entering and leaving Israel.

source.name: Israel Population and Immigration Authority — eVisa-B2 tourist visa: required documents

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published. Applicants for Israel's eVisa-B2 tourist visa must prove sufficient funds with bank statements for the last three months, a bank letter or another document showing the funds.

source.name: Israel Population and Immigration Authority — eVisa-B2 tourist visa: required documents

currencyLimits.text: Israeli rules apply at all crossings: Israel's Tax Authority says anyone entering or leaving Israel must declare the funds in their possession. No official page we could read states the threshold.

source.name: Israel Tax Authority — Requirement to report money brought into or taken out of Israel

notes: The UK's travel advice, which covers Israel and Palestine together, says there are strict rules on goods you can take in or out, and points to the Israeli Tax Authority for the rules on carrying money.

The UK says visitors entering through Ben Gurion Airport get an entry card instead of a passport stamp (other crossings may stamp instead), and to keep the card with your passport until you leave, as you may need it when crossing into Palestine.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to Gaza and to within 500 m of its border, against all travel to the Tulkarm, Jenin and Tubas governorates of the West Bank (except Route 90), and against all but essential travel to the rest of the West Bank apart from East Jerusalem, Bethlehem Governorate, Ramallah Municipality, Jericho municipality and all areas which lie south of it (this includes the Allenby crossing), and some routes.

source.name: UK FCDO — travel advice for the Occupied Palestinian Territories

bestTimeToVisit.text: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit. The CIA World Factbook describes the West Bank's climate as temperate, with warm to hot summers and cool to mild winters, and temperature and rainfall that vary with altitude.

tips.text: The UK says the Israeli authorities control entry to Palestine, and that you must show a passport and Israeli immigration slip to cross between Israel and Palestine. It names Tel Aviv Ben Gurion Airport and the Allenby Bridge crossing with Jordan as entry points.

The UK says the Israeli authorities decide if you can enter Israel, that you may face extra questioning at the border, and that some travellers entering at the Allenby Bridge or Ben Gurion Airport have been given stamps restricting them to 'Palestinian Authority only' or 'Judea and Samaria only'.
Gaza is closed to travellers. The UK says border crossings out of Gaza have been closed to civilians and general traffic since the Israeli military took control of the Rafah crossing on 6 May 2024.

The UK says travellers entering by the Allenby Bridge must pass through Israeli checkpoints and Israeli-controlled territory to reach Jerusalem or Gaza, and to keep your entry card with your passport until you leave, as you may need it when crossing into Palestine.

faq.question: Do I need a visa to visit Palestine?
faq.answer: The Palestinian Authority issues no visas and operates no border control, so entry is governed by Israel's rules. Nationalities that are visa-exempt for Israel — the EU, US, UK, Canada, Australia and many others — need Israel's ETA-IL electronic travel authorization before flying; other nationalities need an Israeli visa from an embassy.

faq.question: How do I get to the West Bank?
faq.answer: Either fly into Israel's Ben Gurion Airport and travel overland, or cross from Jordan over the Allenby (King Hussein) Bridge. Both routes pass Israeli border control.

faq.question: Can tourists visit Gaza?
faq.answer: No. The UK says border crossings out of Gaza have been closed to civilians and general traffic since the Israeli military took control of the Rafah crossing on 6 May 2024, and that consular support is not available inside Gaza.

faq.question: Can Israeli citizens visit Palestinian cities?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states whether, or where, Israeli citizens may enter the West Bank or Gaza.

faq.question: Will visiting the West Bank leave a stamp in my passport?
faq.answer: Not if you fly in: the UK says visitors entering through Ben Gurion Airport get an entry card instead of a passport stamp, while other crossings may give a card or a stamp. Keep the card with your passport until you leave.
